candidate_14.doc_comments:
Benchmark `EliasFano::predecessor` (issue #543 — the ADR-0012 query-time gap).

 `predecessor` is an O(log n) binary search over `get`, with "no sequential
 fast path" per the type's own doc comment. Two query patterns exercise
 that claim directly:
 - `random`: no locality, the worst case.
 - `monotonic`: increasing queries — the shape `LineIndex::to_line_column`
   produces walking a document top to bottom, before any caller-side cache
   (see `benches/line_index.rs` for the cached, end-to-end version).

 Baseline is `Vec<u32>::partition_point`, the same oracle
 `src/text/lines.rs`'s own tests use to check `LineIndex`.

state.issue:
yq: wildcard (`.["a*"]`, `.a*`) and integer (`.[1]`, `has(1)`) mapping-key traversal are not implemented

## Symptom

Real yq routes every mapping-key lookup through `matchKey` (`pkg/yqlib/matchKeyString.go`,
v4.53.3) -- a byte-level glob where `*` is zero or more bytes and `?` exactly one -- and
matches a key by its *text*, so an integer index also finds an `!!int` key. Captured live,
`-o=json -I0`, on `abc: 1\nabd: 2\nx: 3\n1: y\n`:

| filter                      | yq                                    | succinctly                              |
|-----------------------------|---------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| `.["ab*"]`                  | `1` `2`                               | `null`                                  |
| `.ab*`                      | `1` `2`                               | parse error                             |
| `[.["a?c"]]`                | `[1]`                                 | `[null]`                                |
| `[.["*"]] \| length`        | `4`                                   | `1`                                     |
| `.ab* = 9`                  | `{"abc":9,"abd":9,...}`               | parse error                             |
| `del(.["ab*"])`             | `{"x":3,"1":"y"}`                     | unchanged                               |
| `.[1]`                      | `"y"`                                 | `null`                                  |
| `has(1)`                    | `true`                                | `false`                                 |
| `.[1] = "z"`                | `{...,"1":"z"}`                       | `Cannot index object with number`       |
| `has("ab*")`                | `false`                               | `false` (`has` is exact -- agrees)      |
| `.[] \| select(key == "ab*")` | `1` `2`                             | `1` `2` (#2785's `==` already matches)  |

Two quirks worth capturing before implementing, both live on v4.53.3: `del(.["1"])` and
`del(.[1])` on the `1: y` member are **no-ops** (`.["1"]` reads it fine), and `.["x*y"]`
on no match is `null`, not empty.

## Where the code is

- The matcher already exists: `glob::yq_match_key` (`src/jq/glob.rs`, #2785) is the
  byte-for-byte port used by `==`; traversal needs the same function at the key-lookup
  sites (`find_cursor`/`DocumentFields::get` and the `.[n]`-on-object arm), plus a parser
  change for the bare `.ab*` spelling.
- Recorded in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md` under #2785's residuals.

Split out of #2785.
